subject: Feature request for rstan: using binaries or ccache

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Feature request for rstan: using binaries or ccache
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering if it is possible to extend rstan such that one can pass to the stan function the path of a pre-compiled executable binary? As far as I understand each time I restart R, I need to recompile my model. However, some models are used quite frequently and hence it would be more convenient to compile the stan model once and save it as executable binary on disk.

This would save a lot of compilation times - or can this be achieved by the use of ccache (I am not sure if it works with the Rcpp stuff involved here)?

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Feature request for rstan: using binaries or ccache
parts:
If you are using the same machine, it should work to save() the model and then load() it subsequently. Also, ccache has been known to work.

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Feature request for rstan: using binaries or ccache
parts:
R's save/load should work and I think it worked here.  However, what are saved are the samples and the compiled model (ie, the dynamic shared object, AKA dynamic link library).  We cannot save/load the model object (which can be understood as an C++ object) that is created using the dynamic shared object.  So you can use the saved stanfit object to resample, but you cannot call some methods such as get_num_upars. 

--
Jiqiang

First, very nice work on stan! I learn a lot looking at your code. I have a similar issue as Sebastian, if I run
http://pastebin.com/AvxLcm37

If I paste that, then quit R, then start R, and do

library(rstan)
load("saved_fit_school.RData")

schools_dat <- list(J = 8,
                   y = c(28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12),
                   sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18))
fit <- stan(fit = fit, data = schools_dat)
show(get_num_upars(fit)) # 10

that all works for me. Which of those steps doesn't work for you? And what sessionInfo() ?

Ben
